governance.attested_by: neiso-37 weather-floor + daily-basis oil 2026-06-27 (supersedes neiso-33/neiso-36; new NEISO keeper candidate)
governance.note: neiso-37 = the neiso-33 keeper recipe (measured Algonquin/EIA-MA-citygate DAILY gas-hub basis overlay + dual-fuel oil re-attribution + EIA-930-pinned hydro budget with 2024 plant-capacity backfill + biomass/OTHER measured must-run + historic outage overlay + storage vintage ramp) WITH the dual-limb temperature-correlated reliability floor (neiso_temp_reliability_floor) added on top. TWO substantive changes vs the prior runs: (1) it restores the measured daily gas-hub basis overlay (--gas-hub-basis-daily) that neiso-36 accidentally dropped — neiso-36 ran the flat MONTHLY hub overlay, so the within-month cold-day Algonquin spikes never crossed distillate parity, the physical dual-fuel gas->oil switch never tripped, modeled oil collapsed from the measured ~1.6 TWh to ~0.05 TWh and that ~1.5 TWh relabeled back onto gas-CC (gas-family C2 +1.9%->+4.3%, FAIL). With the measured daily overlay restored, the switch trips on the real cold-day prints, 2025 oil returns to 1.60 TWh and the gas family lands at 60.85 vs EIA-930 59.76 (+1.8%, C2 PASS). The daily overlay is forward-faithful and mean-preserving: it replaces the flat monthly hub price with measured Henry Hub daily + measured Algonquin Citygate daily spot prints (EIA Weekly Update) + Transco Z6 NY daily-basis shape fallback, mean-preserved to the measured monthly basis so the annual gas burn/fuel mix is unchanged and only the within-month winter shape is added; the old demand^AGT_DAILY_BASIS_CONVEXITY exponent (which was fitted to the oil burn) was retired 2026-06, so every driver is now measured gas-market data (market_sim.data.fuel.iso_hub_daily_gas_prices). (2) it adds the dual-limb weather floor: a CT_PEAKER summer cooling HOT limb keyed to the NEISO load-weighted daily TMAX, and a COAL + ST_GAS deep-winter COLD limb keyed to TMIN, each holding frac x available capacity over its window. Coefficients regressed from measured CAMPD capacity factors 2023-2025 (cold-limb Spearman rho ~0.35-0.40, hot-limb ~0.47) — physical temperature->commitment rules, NOT TWh-residual fits (scripts/derive_neiso_temp_reliability_floor.py). The floor recovers the weather-reliability commitment energy an energy-only LP leaves on the cheaper CC fleet; in measured-schedule mode it shifts a small amount of energy onto the peakers/steam units (CT_PEAKER 2023/2024 dispatch 0.017/0.002 -> 0.056/0.075 TWh) without changing the demand the LP serves. IMPACT: gas family model 53.44/58.00/60.85 vs EIA-930 grid 52.75/56.92/59.76 (+1.3%/+1.9%/+1.8%, C2 PASS all years); oil 0.35/0.26/1.60 TWh (measured-switch, daily overlay); hydro 8.70/7.33/5.11 TWh (EIA-930 monthly budget pin + 2024 backfill — the 2025 EIA-923 vintage lists only 5 of ~166 hydro plants, so without --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly the LP burns ~5 TWh of phantom gas; both flags are required and both are measured inputs); system mean LMP 34.65/39.16/68.50 vs RT actual 35.70/39.50/65.89 (-2.9%/-0.9%/+4.0%, C3a PASS); CO2 2025 23.67 vs eGRID 23.11 Mt (+2.4%, C5a PASS); C3b price-shape PASS; C4 dispatch correlation PASS. No offer/adder/pin/haircut was added or tuned to a residual. The model is not pinned to either actual. BENCHMARK NOTE: this is the first NEISO bundle scored against the bidirectional vintage reconcile (render_calibration_html.reconcile_vintage_classes), which deflates the EIA-930 gas target by the geothermal+biomass folded into the EIA-930 'Natural Gas' cell (NEISO ~1.6 TWh: model OTHER+biomass 6.41 vs EIA-930 'other' 4.81 in 2023). The prior NEISO keepers (neiso-33/36) were slim bundles whose committed bench predated this reconcile, so their per-class CC_REGULAR benchmark was ~1.7-1.9 TWh too high and the C1 CC_REGULAR over-band item below was masked; against the corrected (deflated) benchmark the current keeper neiso-33 is itself NOT-YET on the same item (C1 CC_REGULAR +1.11/+1.68 TWh, undocumented). neiso-37 is marginally better on it (+1.05/+1.61) and documents it below.
governance.validation_note: Reproducible from the committed bundle: dispatch/<year>_P2.parquet gas-family (CC_REGULAR/CC_CHP/CT_CHP/CT_PEAKER/ST_GAS/ST_CHP) = 54.23/58.81/61.60 TWh raw, oil class = 0.35/0.26/1.60 TWh, hydro = 8.70/7.33/5.11 TWh; system.parquet (pass==P2) simple-mean LMP. Solve command: scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso NEISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --commitment --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly --gas-hub-basis-daily (neiso_temp_reliability_floor default-ON for NEISO). The measured daily basis is logged: 'hub-basis overlay (NEISO 2023/2024/2025, daily): repriced at the measured hub spot ... winter max 30.13/26.69/35.56 $/MMBtu' and 'dual-fuel switching: gas tranches capped at the delivered oil price'. P2 commitment engaged (meta.passes = [P1, P2]). ERCOT/CAISO/MISO/SPP/PJM/NYISO byte-identical (every changed lever is NEISO-gated and backcast-only). Floor coefficients reproduce from scripts/derive_neiso_temp_reliability_floor.py --no-fetch on the archived NOAA series data/raw/neiso-weather/neiso_load_weighted_temp_daily.csv.

exceptions.magnitude: model 51.68 vs deflated EIA-930 grid actual 50.63 TWh (+1.05 TWh, +0.7pp); gas FAMILY 53.44 vs 52.75 (+1.3%, within the C2 ±2.5% band)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (gas-vs-EIA-930-OTHER fold-in categorization, not a model miss)
exceptions.reason: The gas FAMILY is within tolerance (C2 PASS, +1.3%); the per-class C1 gate flags CC_REGULAR because the small family-level surplus concentrates in the marginal combined-cycle unit AND the per-class actual is deflated by the geothermal+biomass that NEISO folds into the EIA-930 'Natural Gas' cell (model OTHER+biomass 6.41 vs EIA-930 'other' 4.81 = ~1.6 TWh fold-in subtracted from the gas target by reconcile_vintage_classes). The model books that OTHER/biomass residual (process gas / landfill / purchased steam) as its own measured must-run rows and serves the un-foldable remainder with marginal CC, so ~1 TWh of the gas the grid attributes to NG-cell-folded non-gas sources lands on CC_REGULAR. This is the same EIA-923-vs-EIA-930 OTHER categorization difference neiso-33's attestation documents for 2025, now visible per-class in 2023 under the bidirectional reconcile. Closable only by reconciling the OTHER/NG-fold-in categorization on both sides, NEVER by injecting the residual or scaling CC to the deflated benchmark (fitting). Carried as the single accepted HARD caveat.

exceptions.magnitude: model 56.27 vs deflated EIA-930 grid actual 54.66 TWh (+1.61 TWh, +1.4pp); gas FAMILY 58.00 vs 56.92 (+1.9%, within the C2 ±2.5% band)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (gas-vs-EIA-930-OTHER fold-in categorization, not a model miss)
exceptions.reason: Same gas-vs-EIA-930-'Natural Gas'-cell fold-in categorization as 2023: the gas family is within the C2 band (+1.9%) but the EIA-930 gas target is deflated by the ~1.6 TWh of geothermal+biomass folded into the NG cell, so the un-foldable OTHER residual served by marginal CC pushes the per-class CC_REGULAR over the tighter C1 per-class volume band. Not a dispatch error; closable only by reconciling the OTHER/NG-fold categorization, not by scaling CC to the deflated benchmark.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (separate structural item: winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity, capped here by the dual-fuel oil-parity)
exceptions.reason: (2023) The model pins every top-price hour at the flat dual-fuel oil-parity cap (~$258.45/MWh): when delivered gas spikes on a cold day, dual-fuel units switch to oil (apply_dual_fuel_pricing) and the marginal price cannot exceed oil parity, so the energy-only LP produces 0 hours > $300. Two faithful ISO-NE scarcity structures were built and tested this session and DO NOT bind in the 2023-25 backcast: (a) in-LP operating-reserve co-optimization on the published NEISO RCPF requirements (neiso_reserve_coopt_inputs / energy_reserve_coopt) and (b) a temperature-dependent winter gas-availability derate (inject_neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate). NEISO is simply not operating-reserve-short in these years -- the ~6.8 GW dual-fuel fleet stays available on oil and imports/hydro/storage/floored-steam keep reserve headroom above the 1,800/1,200 MW requirements even with a 20% cold-window gas derate (reserve_price stays 0), so neither mechanism lifts the price. Both are kept as default-off infrastructure that binds in tighter forecast years. The real residual >$300 driver is winter fuel-INVENTORY scarcity rent (oil/peaker units rationing limited on-site distillate over a multi-day cold snap by bidding above fuel cost) plus reserve scarcity -- and distillate is a liquid global fuel whose COMMODITY price does not spike like pipeline gas basis, so a cold-day oil adder would be a forbidden residual fit. The only forward-faithful way to recover it is to model the oil fleet as inventory-limited (a seasonal oil-burn budget like hydro, whose constraint shadow price IS the scarcity rent, lands on the tightest hours, and is condition-responsive) -- a documented future build, not closable by an adder/offer tune. Accepted caveat.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / reserve-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: Storage arbitrage throughput tracks the peak-to-trough price spread, which is compressed because the LP caps the cold-hour tail at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258, 0 hours > $300; see the price_tail caveat). The reserve co-optimization and gas-availability derate built this session do not widen the spread in the backcast (NEISO is not reserve-short, reserve_price=0, storage 0.73->0.78 TWh), so this is NOT a storage-model error: it closes only when the winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent is recovered via the forward-faithful oil-burn-budget constraint (documented future build), never via a storage or offer tune.
